land.text: the Przemyśl lands of the Rostyslavych, from which Volodymyrko moved his residence to Halych in 1141

predecessors.note: Cliopatria keeps the Peremyshl row to 1146; the Halych page dates the unified principality to 1141 ('effectively establishing a unified Galician principality').

land.text: the Terebovlia lands of Vasylko Rostyslavych, united with Galicia by 1141 (the Terebovlia dossier cites its own page for 1141)

predecessors.note: Cliopatria keeps the Terebovlia row to 1146. Cliopatria's Halych 1147 shape equals Peremyshl 1139 plus Terebovlia 1139 to within two grid cells.

land.text: Galicia, taken by Roman Mstislavich in 1199 after the death of Vladimir II Yaroslavich and united with Volhynia

successors.note: Roman page: 'In 1199 ... captured the Galician throne for the second time' and created the Principality of Galicia-Volhynia. Cliopatria's Halych row runs to 1201 and its Galicia-Volhynia row starts in 1202.

capitals.name: Halych
capitals.note: 'In 1141, Volodymyrko moved his residence from Przemyśl to the more strategically located city of Halych'. Coordinates are the gazetteer's Halych (historic site). Przemyśl, the residence before 1141, belongs to the Peremyshl dossier.

rulers.name: Volodymyrko
rulers.note: Halych page: ruled from 1141, died in 1152.

rulers.name: Yaroslav Osmomysl
rulers.note: Page: the throne passed to him in 1152; the end year 1187 is read from the Vladimir II page, which opens Vladimir's first reign in 1187.

rulers.name: Vladimir II Yaroslavich
rulers.note: First reign 1187-1189 on the Vladimir page; Béla III's page has him flee to Hungary at the end of 1188. The Halych page says Oleg, the designated heir, did not rule; the Vladimir page lists Oleg before Vladimir.

rulers.name: Roman Mstislavich
rulers.title: seized Halych, expelled within the year
rulers.note: 'Roman captured Halych, but was soon expelled by Hungarian king Bela III.'

rulers.name: Andrew (son of Béla III of Hungary)
rulers.title: prince under Hungarian occupation
rulers.note: Béla 'granted control of Halych to Andrew, who was Béla's younger son'; Vladimir expelled him in 1189 or 1190.

rulers.name: Vladimir II Yaroslavich
rulers.note: 'In 1189, with the help of Frederick Barbarossa and the Polish king, Vladimir managed to take Halych'; died 1198 or 1199.

correction.text: the Przemyśl and Terebovlia lands (with Zvenyhorod) under one prince at Halych: 'Volodymyrko moved his residence from Przemyśl to the more strategically located city of Halych, effectively establishing a unified Galician principality'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria opens the Halych row in 1147, but the page dates the unified principality to 1141 and the incorporation of Zvenyhorod to the Berladnyk affair of 1145. Cliopatria's own Peremyshl and Terebovlia rows run to 1146 and sum to the 1147 Halych shape, so the 1141 shape is their union. The page gives no frontier; the infobox gives no area.

106,342 km2 for 1147-1168. The page gives no area (infobox area empty) and no frontier, only that Yaroslav Osmomysl 'consolidated Galician influence in the lower reaches of the Dniester, Prut, and Danube'; the shape reaches 47.1N (the Dniester-Prut lands the Terebovlia dossier says no page dates) and is kept as the best available. Influence on the lower Danube is not territory and is not drawn.
106,207 km2 for 1169-1176, 135 km2 less than the 1147 shape: a grid artefact, no event on the page explains it. Kept.
106,342 km2 for 1177-1187, identical to the 1147 shape. Yaroslav Osmomysl's reign (1152-1187) ends inside this shape; the Cliopatria row stops in 1187 and resumes in 1192.

correction.text: the principality of Halych as in 1177, occupied by Béla III of Hungary from 1188 until Vladimir Yaroslavich retook it in 1189 or 1190

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the years Cliopatria leaves empty (1188-1191, where its 'Halych-Volhynia occupation' row stands instead). Béla page: 'He occupied the Principality of Halych in 1188, but it was lost within two years'; Vladimir returned in 1189 (Vladimir II page) or 1190 (Béla page). Drawn as the 1177 shape with the Hungarian occupation as a ledger event.

correction.text: the same shape, to be drawn 1192-1199 only

keyframe_review.note: The shape is unchanged but its years end in 1199, not 1201: Roman captured Halych in 1199 and united it with Volhynia ('the Principality of Galicia-Volhynia'), and Galicia-Volhynia page infobox: 'Unification of Galicia and Volhynia: 1199'. Cliopatria's 1200-1201 years belong to the Galicia-Volhynia dossier.

region.text: Przemyśl, Terebovlia and Zvenyhorod, the Rostyslavych lands; the page names the cities, not a boundary

ledger.note: 1141: Volodymyrko moves his residence from Przemyśl to Halych and founds the unified Galician principality. 'In 1141, Volodymyrko moved his residence from Przemyśl to the more strategically located city of Halych, effectively establishing a unified Galician principality.' The page gives no founding year for the principality as such and no frontier; Cliopatria starts the row in 1147.
1141: the seat moves from Przemyśl to Halych (destination in identity.capitals).

region.text: the Przemyśl lands, the residence Volodymyrko left in 1141

ledger.note: 1141: Peremyshl is absorbed into the unified principality. The page records the move of residence and the 'unified Galician principality'; the word merger is the researcher's. Cliopatria's Peremyshl row runs to 1146 and should be read as the same land.

region.text: the Terebovlia lands of the Rostyslavych line

ledger.note: 1141: Terebovlia is part of the unified principality. The Halych page lists Terebovlia among the Rostyslavych centres (1084 division; Vasylko confirmed there at Liubech in 1097) and the unified principality from 1141 but does not name the year of its absorption; the Terebovlia dossier dates it to 1141 from its own page.

region.text: Zvenyhorod, incorporated into Galicia after Ivan Berladnyk's defeat; the page gives no extent

ledger.note: 1145: Zvenyhorod is incorporated into Galicia. 'Citizens of Halych backed Ivan Berladnyk's bid for the throne' in 1145 and, after his defeat, Zvenyhorod was incorporated into Galicia (the page gives the year for the Berladnyk episode, not for the incorporation). Cliopatria's 1147 shape equals Peremyshl plus Terebovlia, so it draws no separate Zvenyhorod and the shape does not grow.

region.text: the principality of Halych, occupied by Béla III of Hungary

ledger.note: 1188: Béla III of Hungary occupies Halych. 'He occupied the Principality of Halych in 1188, but it was lost within two years.' Vladimir Yaroslavich 'fled to Hungary at the end of 1188' after a boyar revolt; Roman Mstislavich, who had seized Halych in 1188 (Roman page: 'soon expelled by Hungarian king Bela III'), was expelled and Béla 'granted control of Halych to Andrew, who was Béla's younger son'; Béla styled himself 'King of Galicia'.

1189: Vladimir Yaroslavich retakes Halych. 'In 1189, with the help of Frederick Barbarossa and the Polish king, Vladimir managed to take Halych.' The Béla III page dates his escape from captivity to 'early 1189 or 1190' and has Casimir II of Poland help him expel Andrew; 1189 is the Vladimir page's year.

region.text: Galicia, whose throne Roman captured in 1199

ledger.note: 1199: Roman Mstislavich of Volhynia takes Halych and unites it with Volhynia. 'In 1199, after the death of Prince Volodymyr Yaroslavych of Halych,' Roman 'captured the Galician throne for the second time', creating 'the Principality of Galicia-Volhynia'; the Halych page adds that he seized Halych 'with Leszek the White's support'. Vladimir's death is 1198 or 1199 on the pages. [Reviewer eu-16-d: counterpart changed from principality-of-volhynia to principality-of-galicia-volhynia, the state Roman's union created (Roman page: 'creating the Principality of Galicia-Volhynia'), matching identity.successors and the Volhynia dossier's 1199 merge.]

1199: the Principality of Halych ends in the union with Volhynia as the Principality of Galicia-Volhynia under Roman; the Kingdom of Galicia-Volhynia page's infobox gives 'Unification of Galicia and Volhynia: 1199'.

wars.name: Battle of the Siret River
belligerents: Iziaslav (as the Halych page names him)
wars.outcome: The page records the 1153 battle on the Siret River between Yaroslav Osmomysl's Galicia and Iziaslav; the result and any border change are not in the passage read, so none is recorded.
wars.note: Listed so the reviewer can see it was considered; no territorial result on the page.

wars.name: Hungarian occupation of Halych
wars.outcome: Béla III occupied Halych in 1188 and put his son Andrew on the throne; Vladimir Yaroslavich, helped by the Polish king, returned in 1189 (or 1190 on the Béla page).
wars.note: Roman Mstislavich of Volhynia seized Halych in 1188 and was expelled by Béla within the year (Roman page).

wars.name: Roman Mstislavich's seizure of Halych
wars.outcome: Roman took the Galician throne after Vladimir II Yaroslavich's death and united Halych with Volhynia as the Principality of Galicia-Volhynia.
wars.note: The pages describe a succession seizure, not a campaign with a front; no contest zone is recorded.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier line or a treaty boundary for Halych; the Carpathian, Dniester and Prut limits are approximate and Yaroslav Osmomysl's influence on the lower Danube is not territory.

notes: Pages opened: 5 of a budget of up to 5. Infobox area: the Halych article gives none, so the 106,342 km2 of Cliopatria's shape could not be compared with an infobox figure. START: Cliopatria opens the row in 1147, the page dates the unified principality to 1141 (move of residence to Halych), so the dossier starts in 1141; the Terebovlia dossier ends Terebovlia in 1141 with a merge into Halych, which this dossier mirrors; Peremyshl's dossier (another part of eu-16) should end in 1141 as well. Cliopatria's Peremyshl and Terebovlia rows still run to 1146 and sum to the 1147 Halych shape, so a renderer that honours both will draw the 1141-1146 land twice. END: Cliopatria runs to 1201; the pages give 1199 for the union with Volhynia (the principality-of-galicia-volhynia dossier starts in 1199 too). The Hungarian occupation of 1188-1189 matches Cliopatria's gap 1188-1191 (where its 'Halych-Volhynia occupation' row stands); the Béla III page puts Vladimir's return in early 1189 or 1190, the Vladimir page in 1189. Not settled: the Halych page's infobox 'Succeeded from Peremyshl-Terebovlia Principality / United with Volyn Principality' gives no years; the frontier of Galicia is not on any page opened; 1214 and 1245 events (Hungarian-Polish partition, Daniel's reunion) fall outside this state's life. Needs a dossier: principality-of-zvenyhorod (counterpart of the 1145 gain; Cliopatria has no row); the Kievan Rus', Polish (Sandomierz) and Hungarian dossiers should carry the Halych frontier wars the pages do not detail. Gazetteer: Zvenyhorod is not a gazetteer place (the 1145 gain uses L'viv oblast as a stand-in).
